issues.legal_issue: A maintenance holding forming part of a Saranjam does not pass to an adopted heir against a valid government resumption and fresh grant.
material_facts: The lands had been assigned to a junior family member as a maintenance holding within a Saranjam estate.
After the holder died, the government directed that the holding be continued to his undivided brother, effective from the holder’s death.
The deceased holder’s widow adopted a son without obtaining the government’s sanction.
The adopted son claimed the lands against the brother on the basis of his adoption.
issues.conclusion: The government could resume the maintenance holding and make a fresh grant to the brother; the adoption without government sanction did not displace that grant, and the adopted son was not entitled to the lands under the Saranjam Rules.
issues.legal_principle: The Saranjam Rules, particularly Rules 1, 2, 5, 7 and 8, govern a maintenance holding that forms part of a Saranjam. A Saranjam is held subject to the sovereign’s power to resume it and make a fresh grant; private rights cannot fetter that power. The Court relied on Daulatrao Malojirao v. Province of Bombay (1946) 49 Bom. L.R. 270, which discussed Shekh Sultan Sani v. Shekh Ajmodin (1892) L.R. 20 I.A. 50 and Raghojirao v. Laxmanrao (1912) 14 Bom. L.R. 1226.

rule.if: claim_to_saranjam_maintenance_lands and grant_part_of_saranjam and government_resumed_and_regranted_after_holder_death and adoption_without_government_sanction

predicates.claim_to_saranjam_maintenance_lands: A person in a claim concerning a maintenance holding within a Saranjam asserts entitlement through succession or adoption.
predicates.grant_part_of_saranjam: The holding was treated as part of the Saranjam and subject to its incidents.
predicates.government_resumed_and_regranted_after_h: After the holder died, the government resumed the holding and made a fresh grant to another family member.
predicates.adoption_without_government_sanction: A widow adopted an heir without obtaining the government’s sanction.

issues.definition: When a claim to a maintenance holding forming part of a Saranjam follows a government resumption and fresh grant after the holder’s death, an adoption made without government sanction does not displace that grant.

issues.legal_issue: A claimed family custom of lineal primogeniture does not establish an adopted heir’s title to a maintenance grant unless the custom’s relevant scope and effect are pleaded and proved, including its effect on a later adoption and its binding force against the government.
material_facts: The adopted son relied on an alleged family custom of lineal primogeniture to claim the maintenance lands.
The brother became entitled to the lands on the holder’s death under the asserted rule of primogeniture.
The claim did not plead that a later adoption divested lands that had already vested in the brother.

The alleged custom was not proved with its precise extent, including that it divested the brother’s interest on a later adoption or restricted the government’s power to resume and regrant the holding.
issues.conclusion: The adopted son did not establish title to the lands under the alleged custom.
issues.legal_principle: A party relying on a family custom that departs from ordinary inheritance must plead and prove the custom, its precise extent, and how far it prevails over ordinary law. The claimant also had to establish that the custom bound the government and removed its authority to resume and regrant the maintenance holding. A new case based on divestment by later adoption could not be made for the first time on appeal.

rule.if: claim_to_grant_under_family_custom and custom_of_lineal_primogeniture_claimed and grant_passed_to_relative_on_holder_death and no_custom_proved_divesting_grant_on_later_adoption and no_custom_shown_to_bind_government

predicates.claim_to_grant_under_family_custom: A claimant asserts title to a grant on the basis of a family custom.
predicates.custom_of_lineal_primogeniture_claimed: The claimant relies on a family custom under which property passes by lineal primogeniture.
predicates.grant_passed_to_relative_on_holder_death: On the holder’s death, the grant passed to another relative under the asserted rule.
predicates.no_custom_proved_divesting_grant_on_late: The claimant did not plead and prove a custom under which a later adoption divested the grant from the relative who had received it.
predicates.no_custom_shown_to_bind_government: The claimant did not establish that the custom restricted the government’s authority over the grant.

issues.definition: If a claimant relies on lineal primogeniture after a grant has passed to a relative on the holder’s death, but does not establish a custom that divests that grant on a later adoption and binds the government, the claimant has no title under the custom.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court lacks jurisdiction over a claim against the government relating to Saranjam lands when the claimant must invalidate or overcome a government order concerning those lands to obtain the relief sought.
material_facts: The claimant brought a civil suit seeking possession of lands held as a Saranjam maintenance grant.
The claimant expressly sought a finding that the government’s order granting the lands to another family member was null and ineffective.
Recovery of possession from that family member depended on removing the government order as an obstacle.
The government was a defendant to the claim concerning its order and the Saranjam lands.
issues.conclusion: The claim against the government fell within section 4 of the Bombay Revenue Jurisdiction Act, 1876, and the civil suit was barred.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(a), including its fourth sub-clause, bars civil-court jurisdiction over claims against the government relating to lands granted or held as Saranjam. The Court relied on Mallappa alias Annasaheb Basvantrao Desai Nadgouda v. Tukko Narshimha Mutalik Desai and Others, I.L.R. [1937] Bom. 464, concerning the distinction between claims and suits. A claim that requires the government’s order to be set aside or treated as ineffective is a claim against the government relating to Saranjam lands.

predicates.civil_suit_over_saranjam_lands: A claimant brings a civil suit seeking relief concerning lands held as a Saranjam.
predicates.claim_against_government_concerning_gran: The claimant asks for relief that challenges the government’s decision concerning the grant of those lands.
predicates.relief_depends_on_displacing_government_: The claimant cannot obtain the relief sought unless the government order is set aside or treated as ineffective.

issues.definition: A civil court lacks jurisdiction when a civil suit concerning Saranjam lands includes a claim against the government over the grant and the requested relief depends on displacing a government order.
